$comment: THE KNOWN LIMITATIONS. Canonical, machine-readable, one source. These are carried by the classification claim's basis and by docs/decisions/0011; tests/validation.test.mjs asserts this file and that claim still agree, so neither can quietly drop one. A limitation removed here without evidence is a claim, and it will be treated as one. NOT A ROADMAP: 'what_would_prove_it' says what evidence would be required, not what anyone intends to build.

limitations.not_proven: BRAIN cannot look at arbitrary bytes and determine that they are sensitive.
limitations.why: Every enforcement decision runs on DECLARED provenance -- a class carried by the data and a policy carried by the objective. Nothing inspects content. This was a deliberate choice in round 115: building a classifier would have produced a mechanism whose failures are invisible, and a lane rule that is right most of the time is not a boundary.
limitations.current_behavior: Unlabelled data is treated as PRIVATE, and a payload labelled PUBLIC is released according to that label whether or not the label is correct. Mislabelled data is released correctly per its label, which is the same thing as being released wrongly.
limitations.what_would_prove_it: A classifier with a measured false-negative rate on a corpus BRAIN did not label itself, and an enforcement path that consults it. Neither exists.

limitations.not_proven: Application-level lane enforcement cannot contain malicious code running inside the same process.
limitations.why: The gate governs code that asks it. Hostile in-process code does not have to ask: it can import node:http and open its own socket. No amount of checking inside the same process changes that, because the check and the bypass have equal privilege.
limitations.current_behavior: Enforced against BRAIN's own paths, against trusted adapters using the provided send path, and against buggy adapters that ask and mishandle the answer -- the gate refuses first, so a mishandled denial still sends nothing. A test in tests/laneenforcement.test.mjs performs the bypass deliberately and succeeds.
limitations.what_would_prove_it: An external runtime boundary: a separate OS process with no network access (namespace, container, or firewall rule), or a capability-based runtime where the network is not ambiently reachable. That is an operating-system property, not an application one.

limitations.not_proven: Reuse is not sensitive to how many independent roots support a belief.
limitations.why: The sufficiency basis fingerprints the semantic outcome -- belief, epistemic state, controlling authority. Adding supporting records to the fingerprint was tried in round 114 and made every reread invalidate every reuse, so the fingerprint was narrowed and the gap documented rather than hidden.
limitations.current_behavior: A belief that keeps its value while losing one of two independent supporting roots reports STILL_VALID. The answer is unchanged and genuinely weaker, and BRAIN does not say so.
limitations.what_would_prove_it: A strength measure in the basis that distinguishes losing a root from gaining an unrelated record, with tests showing it does not invalidate on ordinary rereads.

limitations.not_proven: A one-time grant consumed on both sides of a partition cannot be prevented from being consumed twice.
limitations.why: At-most-once across disconnected worlds is not establishable by merging afterwards. The two consumptions both really happened, in worlds that could not see each other; no merge rule invents a winner without inventing a story.
limitations.current_behavior: DETECTION, NOT PREVENTION. Rejoin reports both consumptions intact, names the conflict, and states that coordination before the partition is what would have prevented it.
limitations.what_would_prove_it: Coordination established BEFORE the partition -- a lease, a quorum, or a single-writer token. Every one of those trades availability for the guarantee, and none is implemented.

limitations.not_proven: Nothing about multi-owner or multi-tenant operation has been tested.
limitations.why: Every round measured one owner on one machine. Lanes separate kinds of work for one owner; they were never asked to separate two owners from each other, and a mechanism is only proven against the question it was asked.
limitations.current_behavior: Single owner. `authority:owner.classification` names one owner and nothing arbitrates between two. Lane enforcement runs on declared provenance, which no adversarial tenant was ever invited to declare.
limitations.what_would_prove_it: An adversarial tenant model: two owners with conflicting authority over the same subject, and tests showing neither can read, write, or release the other's records.
